rp-dry-01.back: 335 to 900 m; 280 to 500 mm a year. The driest, warmest forest zone.

rp-dry-02.back: About 350 to 1,450 m; 300 to 750 mm a year.

rp-dry-06.front: Why were dry pine forests open?
rp-dry-06.back: Frequent ground fires killed small trees and brush; thick barked old trees lived.

rp-dry-07.front: Mean fire interval at Trout Creek near Summerland, 1715 to 1952?

rp-dry-08.back: Dense thickets of young trees filled in, cutting views and feed.

rp-dry-10.front: When do fir needles peak in Kamloops mule deer diet?

rp-dry-11.back: Big sagebrush, pasture sage, bitterbrush, rabbitbrush, snowbrush, saskatoon, rose, serviceberry and Douglas fir.

rp-dry-12.front: Mule deer year in dry forest country?
rp-dry-12.back: Often high in September; moving down October and November; low PP and IDF south slopes December to March.

rp-dry-13.front: Ground plants of a dry IDF floor?
rp-dry-13.back: Bluebunch wheatgrass, kinnikinnick, soopolallie, spirea, saskatoon.

rp-dry-14.front: Midday in open dry forest: where are deer?
rp-dry-14.back: Bedded on benches, heads of draws, shady north edges, under big fir.
